messages.subject: Re: geom_segment in coord_polar, missing segments
parts:
I see it too; it's got to be a bug somewhere. Here is what I have
figured out about it so far.

It is not a coincidence that the missing segment is the last one in df.
(That appears to be a necessary, but not sufficient, condition). I can
make this happen with a subset of the data, and it is dependent of the
range of the x-axis.

Using your df and p:

# relevant segment
df[17, ]
## x xend y
## 17 83.5 83 5
# x range, by default:
range(c(df[1:17, "x"], df[1:17, "xend"]), na.rm = TRUE)
## [1] 24.6 84.5

# segment present
p %+% df[1:17,] + expand_limits(x=10.25) + coord_polar()
# segment absent
p %+% df[1:17,] + expand_limits(x=10.2) + coord_polar()

# segment present
p %+% df[1:17,] + scale_x_continuous(limits=c(10.25, 84.5)) + coord_polar()
# segment absent
p %+% df[1:17,] + scale_x_continuous(limits=c(10.2, 84.5)) + coord_polar()

As you can see, it is very sensitive to what the trained range of x is,
though it does not seem to matter whether it comes from another layer
(via expand_limits) or from the scale itself (via limits argument).

Digging more:

pg <- p %+% df[1:17, ] + scale_x_continuous(limits = c(10.25, 84.5)) +
coord_polar()
pb <- p %+% df[1:17, ] + scale_x_continuous(limits = c(10.2, 84.5)) +
coord_polar()

pgb <- ggplot_build(pg)
pbb <- ggplot_build(pb)

all.equal(pgb, pbb)
## [1] "Component 2: Component 3: Component 1: Component 6: Mean
relative difference: 0.004878"
## [2] "Component 2: Component 5: Component 1: Component 1: Mean
relative difference: 0.004878"
names(pbb)[2]
## [1] "panel"
names(pbb[[2]])[3]
## [1] "x_scales"
names(pbb[[2]][[3]])[1]
## NULL
names(pbb[[2]][[3]][[1]])[6]
## [1] "limits"
pbb[[2]][[3]][[1]][[6]]
## [1] 10.2 84.5
pgb[[2]][[3]][[1]][[6]]
## [1] 10.25 84.50


So looking at the first stage of the build (ggplot_build), the only
difference is in the limits of the scales. Go to the next stage (this
gets verbose):


pgt <- ggplot_gtable(pgb)
## Warning: Removed 1 rows containing missing values (geom_segment).
pbt <- ggplot_gtable(pbb)
## Warning: Removed 1 rows containing missing values (geom_segment).

The string mis-matches are differences in names of the grobs and can be
ignored. Differences 27-29 deal with the x-axis. The real issues are in
31-34 which are pulled out for comparison. The differ in there length by
1, which is the one missing segment. So where is isolated, now just why.

I chased down the drawing code for awhile and it seems fine through
GeomSegment$draw (pieces is right at the end of GeomSegment$draw), at
least until the handoff to GeomPath$draw at which point I got lost
around the coord_munch call. I couldn't keep going when I hit that, but
that seems at least a suspicious place that there might be problems
since it can drop points from a polar plot in certain (?) circumstances.

Sorry I don't have any advice to help you fix the plot. Hopefully what
I've done should allow someone else to figure out what is really wrong.

messages.subject: Re: geom_segment in coord_polar, missing segments
parts:
On 6/20/2013 12:42 PM, Brian Diggs wrote:
> On 6/19/2013 5:11 PM, Didac Santesmasses wrote:
>> Hi,
>>
>> I'm trying to plot a tree structure using geom_segment in coord_polar.
>> When the polar coordinates are applied, all the segments are visible.
>> However, when the limits of x axis are modified, some of the segments
>> disappear.
>>
>> Has anyone found anything similar?
>>

[...much example and discussion trimmed...]

I figured out what was the bug was. It had to do with when the final
segment was short enough not to need interpolating to be a curve in
polar coordinates. In that case, the segment was dropped (well, one end
of it was). I've submitted a pull request to fix it:
https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/pull/823

If you need the fix sooner than when it will be released, you can just
used the modified versions of interp and munch_data in that pull
request, or you can install my branch of it (using devtools):

install_github("ggplot2", "BrianDiggs", ref="fix/munch")

or

install_github("ggplot2", "hadley", pull=823)

--
Brian S. Diggs, PhD
Senior Research Associate, Department of Surgery
Oregon Health & Science University
